title: Sell in-the-money covered calls when downside protection matters
summary: Covered call premium is downside protection. When a stock is at all-time highs and looks rich, protection matters more than upside. An in-the-money covered call has intrinsic and extrinsic value and protects dollar for dollar down to the strike. The speaker compares a 70 delta covered call with a 30 delta one.

steps.caption: The stock is at all-time highs, $100. You care more about the downside than the upside.
The 70 delta covered call at $95: big premium, intrinsic plus extrinsic. Protection is dollar for dollar down to the strike.
The 30 delta covered call at $105: smaller premium, more upside if the stock rallies.
The difference: the ITM call gives up upside for much more downside protection.
The ITM call's breakeven is much lower, so it absorbs a larger drop.

takeaways: Covered call premium is your downside protection.
When the stock looks rich, an ITM covered call protects more than an OTM one.
Expect assignment if the stock stays above the ITM strike; roll or close if you want to keep the shares.
caveats: Stock legs conflict with the owner's options-only rule; a deployment needs an override.
The claim that this beats collars or long puts is the speaker's view, not tested here.

backtest.note: Monthly 70-delta in-the-money covered calls on stock near highs.
